source_title: NSW bushfires: Hunter Valley fires which left homes ablaze being treated as 'very suspicious' (ABC News, 18 Jan 2017)
quote: although some sheds and outbuildings had been damaged, no homes were destroyed
match_note: Applies to the Kurri Kurri / Heddon Greta bushfires of 18 Jan 2017 (Cessnock LGA, ~650-680 ha). The dataset's r16 fires (Forbes Street 13 Dec 2016 1,167 ha; George Downes Dr; Cave Arm; Finchley Track; Cessnock St) are not named in the source, and the brief says the Kurri Kurri flare-up is also declared separately as r22 (2017-01-18). So this is direct evidence for the Jan 2017 Kurri Kurri fires and only indirect (same council, same summer) for r16. RFS 2016/17 annual report p.28 says December 2016 had 'only one significant fire event' (Urana, Clear Hills Rd), which is consistent with no big Dec 2016 Cessnock fire but is not a loss statement. Quote came from WebFetch (small-model) output, re-check on the page if it matters.

source_title: Assessment of last week's fire affected areas completed (NSW RFS media release, 18 Feb 2017)
quote: NSW RFS Building Impact Assessment Teams have confirmed a total of 45 homes were destroyed in the fires
match_note: INFERENCE BY ACCOUNTING, not an explicit 'no homes lost' sentence. RFS declared the assessment of the 11-12 Feb 2017 fires 'completed'; the five itemised fires sum exactly to the 45 total (Sir Ivan 35, Pappinbarra 6, Dondingalong 2, Boggabri 1, White Cedars 1) and none is in Mid-Coast (Pappinbarra is Port Macquarie-Hastings). Barnards Road (Gloucester) and the other Mid-Coast fires named in r23 (Wardells/Gloucester Tops Rd 4 Feb, Mount Pleasant Rd 4 Feb, Howes Creek 5 Feb) appear in no RFS damage-assessment update (checked Updates 3, 7, 9 and Final). Weak point: those fires started 4-7 Feb, before the assessed weekend, and 9 of the season's 65 homes are unallocated (see notes), so a loss there cannot be strictly excluded. Drop this row if you want explicit statements only.
